verdicts.title: A counterexample to the Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture and related problems
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Consider a graph obtained by taking edge disjoint union of $k$ complete bipartite graphs. Alon, Saks and Seymour conjectured that such graph has chromatic number at most $k+1$. This well known conjecture remained open for almost twenty years. In this paper, we construct a counterexample to this conjecture and discuss several related problems in combinatorial geometry and communication complexity.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses a counterexample to the Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture about chromatic numbers of edge-disjoint unions of bipartite graphs, with mentions of 'combinatorial geometry and communication complexity' as related areas, but makes no claim about CNF satisfiability, Coxeter diagrams, or entropy-based lower bounds on communication complexity.
